<meta>continues from previous page: the speech of Karna expressing his determination to defeat the enemy.</meta>

"In every way, I shall conquer all the gathered Pandavas <note>the five sons of Pandu</note> today." 58

Duryodhana spoke:
"I will do all of this just as you think best, O Karna. Wagons filled with quivers shall follow you closely, O son of a Suta <note>Karna was raised by a charioteer or Suta</note>. 59
Let carts carry iron arrows and feathered shafts for you."

<column-break/>

"We and all the kings shall follow you, O Karna." 60

Sanjaya <note>the narrator and visionary advisor to King Dhritarashtra</note> spoke:
"Having spoken thus, O Great King, your powerful son, the King <note>Duryodhana</note>, approached the King of Madra <note>Shalya</note> and spoke these words." 61

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the Book of Karna of the glorious Mahabharata.<-

---

## 23

Sanjaya spoke:
"Your son, O Great King, having approached the King of Madra <note>Shalya</note> with humility, spoke these words out of affection. 1
'O you who are true to your vows, O highly fortunate one, O you who increase the grief of your enemies!'"

<column-break/>

---

<summary>Duryodhana agrees to support Karna with supplies and troops before approaching Shalya, the King of Madra, with a humble request. This marks the transition between chapters 22 and 23 of the Book of Karna.</summary>
